topic.title: Graph Construction and Label-Efficient Learning
topic.overview: Graph-based learning uses relationships among examples to spread information from a limited labeled set. The graph itself is a modeling choice: edges, weights, anchors, kernels, and coarse representations determine which observations influence each other. Selecting labels and constructing that structure are therefore closely connected tasks.
topic.whyItMatters: A scalable but misleading graph can propagate mistakes widely. Useful methods need to preserve relevant neighborhoods while reducing memory and deciding which labels provide the most information about the unlabeled remainder.
topic.evolution: Early representatives use diffusion kernels and biological pathway graphs. Anchor-based construction later makes large sparse graphs practical, followed by learned propagation and asymmetric graph designs. Recent work adds approximation guarantees for selecting a fixed label budget and studies graph coarsening. The common question is how to retain predictive structure with limited labels and computation.
openQuestions: How can graph construction be validated when labels are scarce?
Which label-selection guarantees survive misspecified or changing graph relationships?

papers.tldr: CutSSL uses a continuous graph-partitioning formulation with provably integer solutions to improve learning with scarce or imbalanced labels.

papers.title: Efficient Streaming Algorithms for Graphlet Sampling
papers.tldr: Semi-streaming algorithms sample independent uniform graphlets from large graphs with a near-optimal tradeoff between memory and sequential passes.

papers.title: GraphCL: Graph-based Clustering for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
papers.tldr: GraphCL combines local image features and their pairwise relationships through graph-based clustering to improve semi-supervised medical image segmentation.

papers.title: Scalable Sobolev IPM for Probability Measures on a Graph
papers.tldr: A regularized Sobolev metric on graphs admits fast closed-form computation and supports positive-definite kernels for comparing distributions.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Parametric Generalized Category Discovery on Graphs
papers.tldr: A Wasserstein-based analysis identifies necessary conditions for graph category discovery and motivates the experimentally supported SWIRL method.

papers.title: A CLT for Polynomial GNNs on Community-Based Graphs
papers.tldr: Under a growing-degree community graph model, polynomial GNN embeddings approach Gaussian mixtures whose collapse with depth precisely characterizes oversmoothing.

papers.title: Adjusted Count Quantification Learning on Graphs
papers.tldr: Two graph-aware methods improve label-distribution estimation under structural shifts and connections between differently labeled vertices.

papers.title: Adversarial Graph Fusion for Incomplete Multi-view Semi-supervised Learning with Tensorial Imputation
papers.tldr: AGF-TI combines adversarial graph fusion and low-rank tensor reconstruction to address structural fragmentation caused by missing views.

papers.title: Geometric Imbalance in Semi-Supervised Node Classification
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes geometric ambiguity affecting minority graph classes and introduces a framework that improves classification under imbalance.

papers.title: Graph–Smoothed Bayesian Black-Box Shift Estimator and Its Information Geometry
papers.tldr: A graph-smoothed Bayesian label-shift estimator jointly models class proportions and classifier uncertainty, with theoretical estimation guarantees.

papers.title: Harnessing Feature Resonance under Arbitrary Target Alignment for Out-of-Distribution Node Detection
papers.tldr: RSL detects unfamiliar graph nodes through differences in feature movement during training, without requiring a supervised pretext classification task.

papers.title: Low-Rank Graphon Learning for Networks
papers.tldr: The paper jointly models graphons and connection probability matrices with low rank, enabling efficient estimation with a consistency guarantee.

papers.title: Semi-supervised Vertex Hunting, with Applications in Network and Text Analysis
papers.tldr: Semi-supervised vertex hunting uses transformed partial coordinate information to recover simplex structure with faster theoretical convergence than unsupervised alternatives.

papers.title: Spectral Graph Coarsening Using Inner Product Preservation and the Grassmann Manifold
papers.tldr: The method coarsens graphs by preserving inner products among node features, improving both coarsening measures and node-classification results.

papers.title: Taxonomy of reduction matrices for Graph Coarsening
papers.tldr: Allowing reduction matrices beyond pseudo-inverses can decrease signal loss for a fixed graph coarsening.

papers.title: An Approximation Algorithm for Graph Label Selection
papers.tldr: The paper gives a provable approximation for selecting graph labels within a fixed budget and practical variants that scale to larger graphs.

papers.title: HSMAD: Heterophily-Driven Spectral and Manifold Learning for Graph Anomaly Detection
papers.tldr: HSMAD uses differences between connected nodes to guide spectral filtering and geometric representations for graph anomaly detection.
